title: Longest Arithmetic Subsequence
goal: Find the longest arithmetic subsequence with one constant consecutive difference.
strategy: Each ending index owns a map from difference to best length. A pair extends an earlier subsequence with the same difference, or begins a new two-element subsequence when none exists.

phasePurposes.start: Find the longest arithmetic subsequence with one constant consecutive difference.
phasePurposes.inspect: Each ending index owns a map from difference to best length. A pair extends an earlier subsequence with the same difference, or begins a new two-element subsequence when none exists.
phasePurposes.update: Each ending index owns a map from difference to best length. A pair extends an earlier subsequence with the same difference, or begins a new two-element subsequence when none exists.
phasePurposes.done: Find the longest arithmetic subsequence with one constant consecutive difference.

edgeCases: Repeated equal values use difference zero
A descending arithmetic chain uses a negative difference
Two values always form an arithmetic subsequence
